full: Project POLLUX — Member-State Exposure Reporting Portal
line: CASTOR made the lending data clean. Nobody outside Lending Operations can see it. POLLUX builds the portal that shows exposure by member state, instrument and maturity — and it is built the PM²-Agile way, because nobody agrees what the report should contain.
money: Approved in the Business Case. PM²-Agile still has a Business Case and a Charter — that is the point of Act 1.
Reported at administrative closure on 20 Mar 2030.
26 iterations. 4 releases. Daily Stand-up every morning at 09:30.
Plus two seconded contractor members from Levallois Systems.
sc: Time to deliver a new report view
Manually maintained spreadsheets in the reporting chain
Figures traceable to the lending platform without manual mapping
Open internal-audit findings on reporting version control
dates: Business Case and Project Charter approved
Development Handbook and Development Work Plan baselined
Release 1 — exposure by member state, read-only
Release 2 — instrument and maturity views, reconciliation panel
who: PM²-Agile does not delete the Project Manager. You still hold the gates, the Business Case and the four logs.
Head of Reporting. Owns the Work Items List and decides what gets built first. Her acceptance criteria are not negotiable.
The Business Analyst from CASTOR, promoted. Facilitates the ceremonies. Not a manager of people.
Seconded from Enterprise Architecture. Every enabler story starts with him asking what problem is being solved.
Developer. Consistently underestimated and consistently right about the hard technical problem.
Data engineer. Builds the engine — and famously never finished one, which is a live risk.
Seconded lead from Levallois. Contractually precise about what 'done' means.
Unchanged from CASTOR. Represents the Project Owner in the room; collides with Curie over Release 2.
Unchanged. Still accountable for the benefits.
Unchanged. Still accountable for the deliverables.
Still asks what leaves the portfolio — and why he should fund something that cannot say what it will deliver.
Delighted, because retrospectives are his life's work.
Quietly appalled that nobody wants a Gantt chart. There is still a schedule — three of them.
conv: A number that says 'this is about twice that'. The team's scale is 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21. Points never convert to days.
Started at an invented 34, revised to 30 once real iterations had run. Used to forecast, never as a target.
Iteration 1 starts 8 Jan 2029. The length never moves; the scope does.

A shared quality standard for the team, revised through the agreed process and recorded in the Development Handbook. Apply the agreed version consistently. Acceptance criteria describe the needs of an individual work item.
per work item, written by the Product Owner
A story can pass every acceptance criterion and still not be Done.
numbered on the Work Items List
Item 127, item 131. Cards on the long wall, ordered by the Product Owner.
Characters quote them by line number. Line 1 = deliver early and continuously. Line 9 = simplicity. Line 12 = be enterprise-aware.
rooms: Third floor, the old training room
One long wall, a smell of whiteboard marker, and twelve printed lines taped at eye height.
The board, the build screen, the stand-up at 09:30.
Iteration Planning, Review, Retrospective. The Work Items List runs down the wall.
The same room CASTOR started in. Gates happen here.
Medici, and the Deputy Managing Director's office.
